quote: Repeated mechanostimulation leads to severe alterations of the plant morphology, like dwarfism, pithiness, altered mechanical properties of stem, delayed flowering, improved anchorage strength of roots, and reduced stomatal aperture
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch).

value: many legumes fold their leaflets at nightfall and open them in the morning; in the rain tree Samanea saman the hinge channel genes follow a daily clock

source.authors: Mano H, Hasebe M
source.title: Rapid movements in plants

quote: In many leguminous species, pulvini participate in daily leaf movements in which the compound leaf folds its leaflets at the beginning of the night and unfolds them in the morning
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). new trait: daily clock (period, what sets it, what it gates); no existing key fits.

value: shoots sense their angle of tilt, and the response does not change with the strength of gravity from 0.1 g to 3 g
method: centrifuge with growth-kinematics imaging, four flowering-plant species

source.authors: Chauvet H, Pouliquen O, Forterre Y, Legué V, Moulia B
source.title: Inclination not force is sensed by plants during shoot gravitropism

quote: we show that shoot gravitropic responses to steady levels of gravity in four representative angiosperm species is independent of gravity intensity. All gravitropic responses tested are dependent only on the angle of inclination from the direction of gravity.
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). new trait: gravity sensing (statoliths, angle, timing); no existing key fits. Range 0.1 to 3 g from the Results.

value: the bending response follows the sine of the tilt: none when upright, greatest when horizontal, none when upside down

source.authors: Chauvet H, Pouliquen O, Forterre Y, Legué V, Moulia B
source.title: Inclination not force is sensed by plants during shoot gravitropism

quote: The gravitropic response increased almost linearly from zero for θinit = 0, to reach a maximum of approx. 0.6 around θinit = 90° and decreased back to zero for higher inclination angles
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). new trait: gravity sensing (statoliths, angle, timing); no existing key fits.

value: gravity is sensed by starch grains (statoliths) that settle to the lower side of special cells; wind and rain shake shoots with up to 3 g
method: review statement in a primary paper

source.authors: Chauvet H, Pouliquen O, Forterre Y, Legué V, Moulia B
source.title: Inclination not force is sensed by plants during shoot gravitropism

quote: When the plant is inclined, the statoliths sediments in the direction of the gravity inside the statocyte3. A redistribution of auxin transporters is then triggered in the statocyte4.
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). new trait: gravity sensing (statoliths, angle, timing); no existing key fits. The 3 g of wind and rain is in the Results (citing ref. 23).

value: sensing the angle, not the force, keeps a shoot's direction steady while wind shakes it

source.authors: Chauvet H, Pouliquen O, Forterre Y, Legué V, Moulia B
source.title: Inclination not force is sensed by plants during shoot gravitropism

quote: This contrasts with the otolith system in the internal ear of vertebrates and explains the robustness of the control of growth direction by plants despite perturbations like wind shaking.
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). new trait: gravity sensing (statoliths, angle, timing); no existing key fits.

value: seed-plant roots bend to gravity fast; lycophyte and fern roots bend slowly and moss rhizoids more slowly still
method: root bending after 90 degree reorientation across lineages

source.authors: Zhang Y, Xiao G, Wang X, Zhang X, Friml J
source.title: Evolution of fast root gravitropism in seed plants

quote: Lycophytes and ferns have a true root, but the model lycophyte Selaginella moellendorffii and the model fern Ceratopteris richardii showed much slower gravitropism than the roots of the flowering plants
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). new trait: gravity sensing (statoliths, angle, timing); no existing key fits.

value: after a root is tipped, auxin carriers in the gravity-sensing cells move to the new lower side within minutes
method: review statement in a primary paper

source.authors: Zhang Y, Xiao G, Wang X, Zhang X, Friml J
source.title: Evolution of fast root gravitropism in seed plants

quote: Following a gravitropic stimulus, AtPIN3 and AtPIN7 rapidly relocalize laterally within the first few minutes to facilitate the asymmetrical auxin redistribution between the upper and lower parts of the root
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). new trait: gravity sensing (statoliths, angle, timing); no existing key fits.

value: leaves played the vibrations of a chewing caterpillar raise their defences against the next attack, and the plants tell chewing from wind and insect song
method: vibration playback for 2 h through an actuator on the leaf

source.authors: Appel HM, Cocroft RB
source.title: Plants respond to leaf vibrations caused by insect herbivore chewing

quote: Arabidopsis thaliana (L.) rosettes pre-treated with the vibrations caused by caterpillar feeding had higher levels of glucosinolate and anthocyanin defenses when subsequently fed upon by Pieris rapae (L.) caterpillars than did untreated plants.
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). Also from the abstract: the plants discriminated chewing from wind and insect song.

method: playback; laser vibrometry of petals; nectar sugar measured after 3 min

source.authors: Veits M, Khait I, Obolski U, Zinger E, Boonman A, Goldshtein A, Saban K, Seltzer R, Ben-Dor U, Estlein P, Kabat A, Peretz D, Ratzersdorfer I, Krylov S, Chamovitz D, Sapir Y, Yovel Y, Hadany L
source.title: Flowers respond to pollinator sound within minutes by increasing nectar sugar concentration

quote: Oenothera drummondii flowers, exposed to playback sound of a flying bee or to synthetic sound signals at similar frequencies, produce sweeter nectar within 3 min
note: Full text in the literature collection (plants-touch). Low-frequency signal 50 to 1000 Hz; sugar 19.8% and 19.1% after Low and Bee sound against 16.3% and 16.0% after silence and 158-160 kHz. The petals vibrate with the sound.
